# Jubilees Chapter 4 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Cain and Abel; Seth; Enoch

---

**4:1** In the third week of the second jubilee Eve bore Cain; in the fourth week she bore Abel; and in the fifth week she bore her daughter Awan.

**4:2** In the first year of the third jubilee, Cain killed Abel, because God had accepted Abel's sacrifice and had not accepted Cain's offering.

**4:3** He killed him in the field, and Abel's blood cried out from the ground to heaven, accusing him of the slaying.

**4:4** The LORD reproved Cain on account of Abel whom he had killed, and made him a fugitive on the earth because of his brother's blood, and cursed him on the earth.

**4:5** On this account it is written on the heavenly tablets: "Cursed is the one who strikes his neighbor treacherously; and let all who have seen or heard say, Amen; and the man who has seen and has not declared it, let him be cursed just as the one who committed it."

**4:6** For this reason we reported to the LORD our God what Cain had done — that he had killed Abel — so that it would never be concealed again.

**4:7** He was judged to be in darkness and to be cast out from before the face of God, because he had killed Abel.

**4:8** He was permitted to see light no more. He dwelt in the land of Naid, the land where Adam had been placed to live.

**4:9** There he built a city and named it after his son Enoch.

**4:10** Adam knew his wife again, and she bore him a son. He named him Seth, saying: "God has raised up another offspring for us on the earth in place of Abel, for Cain slew him."

**4:11** In the sixth week Adam begat his daughter Azura.

**4:12** Cain took his sister Awan as his wife, and she bore him Enoch at the close of the fourth jubilee. In the first year of the first week of the fifth jubilee, houses were built on the earth, and Cain built a city.

**4:13** Enoch took as his wife Mualet, daughter of Madai son of Jared — one of those daughters born after the death of Abel.

**4:14** She bore him Irad; Irad fathered Mehujael; Mehujael fathered Methushael; Methushael fathered Lamech.

**4:15** In the eleventh jubilee, in the fourth week, Jared took a wife named Baraka, daughter of Rasujal, a daughter of his father's brother. She bore him a son in the fifth week, in the fourth year of the jubilee, and he named him Enoch.

**4:16** Enoch was the first among men born on earth to learn writing and knowledge and wisdom, and he wrote down the signs of heaven according to the order of their months in a book, so that people might know the seasons of the years according to the order of their months.

**4:17** He was the first to write a testimony. He testified to the sons of men among the generations of the earth, recounted the weeks of the jubilees, made known to them the days of the years, set in order the months, and recounted the sabbatical years, as these were made known to him.

**4:18** In the visions of his sleep he saw what was and what will be — everything that will come upon the children of men in their generations until the day of judgment. He saw all things, understood them, and wrote his testimony, and placed the testimony on earth for all the children of men and for their generations.

**4:19** In the twelfth jubilee, in the seventh week, he took a wife named Edna, daughter of Danel, a daughter of his father's brother. In the sixth year of that week she bore him a son, and he named him Methuselah.

**4:20** Moreover, he lived with the angels of God for six jubilees of years, and they showed him everything on earth and in the heavens, the rule of the sun, and he wrote down all of it.

**4:21** He testified against the Watchers who had sinned and against the sons of men. His testimony is written as evidence against them. He recorded all their deeds: the deeds of the Watchers and of their sons and their wives — how they were corrupted, how they sinned, their punishment, and their condemnation. He wrote it all.

**4:22** He was taken from among the children of men, and we brought him into the garden of Eden with great honor. There he writes the condemnation and judgment of the world, and all the wickedness of the children of men.

**4:23** Because of this, God brought the waters of the flood upon all the land of Eden; for Enoch was placed there as a sign and witness against all the children of men, to recount all the deeds of the generations until the day of condemnation.

**4:24** And he offered the incense of the sanctuary — sweet spices acceptable before the LORD — on the mountain.

**4:25** For there are four places on the face of the earth that belong to the LORD: the garden of Eden, the Mountain of the East, this mountain on which you now stand — Mount Sinai — and Mount Zion, which will be sanctified in the new creation as the sanctification of the earth. Through these four places the earth will be sanctified from all its guilt and uncleanness throughout the generations of the world.

**4:26** In the fourteenth jubilee, in the third week, in the first year of that week, Methuselah took a wife named Edna, daughter of Azrial. She bore him a son in the first year of the fifth week, and he named him Lamech.

**4:27** In the fifteenth jubilee, in the third week, in the third year, Lamech took a wife named Betenos. She bore him a son, and he named him Noah, saying: "This one will comfort us in our work and in the toil of our hands on the earth which the LORD has cursed."

**4:28** At the close of the nineteenth jubilee, in the seventh week, in the sixth year, Adam died. All his sons buried him in the land of his creation, and he was the first to be buried in the earth.

**4:29** He lacked seventy years of one thousand years, for one thousand years are as one day in the testimony of the heavens. Therefore it was written concerning the tree of knowledge: "On the day you eat of it you shall die." He did not complete that full day, for he died within it.

**4:30** At the close of that jubilee, Cain was killed after him in the same year, for his house fell upon him and he died in its ruins, killed by its stones — for with a stone he had killed Abel, and so by a stone he was killed in righteous judgment.

**4:31** For this reason it is ordained on the heavenly tablets: with the same instrument with which a man kills his neighbor shall he be killed; in the manner he wounded him, so shall they deal with him.

**4:32** In the twenty-fifth jubilee, in the fifth week, in the first year, Noah took a wife named Emzara, daughter of Rake'el, a daughter of his father's brother. In the third year she bore him Shem; in the fifth year, Ham; and in the first year of the sixth week, Japheth.

---
*SOPHIA notes: Consensus follows LOGOS throughout. Enoch's sevenfold role (writing, calendar, prophecy, angelic companion, Watcher-witness, temple priest, Eden guardian) carefully preserved. "Visions of his sleep" (v.18) retained as technical term for prophetic dream. Four holy mountains (v.25) preserved as named.*
